title: fix: preserve committed debit amounts when credit side-effects fail
author: sharktide
pr_body_excerpt:
- Preserves the actual wallet debit when subsequent API-key budget reconciliation or developer/community credits fail. Uses ordinary error logs only—no new Tinybird events, error types or caller plumbing.
- Keeps pre-debit failures, reservation release, prices, owner exemptions and rounding unchanged. Does not retry charges or add automatic credit recovery.
- Tests three focused real-D1 failure cases and extends the existing realtime regression to verify the recorded charge without charging twice.
- Validation: 166 tests pass across five relevant Gen files; Gen typecheck and Biome pass. Changes only three files, with no net increase in runtime code.

Fixes #14679

gist.headline: The ledger keeps its pollen
gist.blurb: A charge that made it out of the wallet now stays recorded, even if the later credit bookkeeping stumbles over a root. The hive gets one honest receipt, not a second sting.
gist.summary: Billing now preserves the committed wallet debit when API-key budget reconciliation or developer/community credit side-effects fail, while leaving pre-debit failures, reservation release, owner exemptions, prices, and rounding unchanged.
gist.impact: Users and developers get an accurately recorded single charge in these partial-failure cases, with no automatic retry or duplicate debit.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy garden ledger station: Polli carefully stamps a completed pollen debit into a glowing ledger while a few smaller side-accounting tubes gently sputter nearby, making the distinction between the committed charge and optional follow-up credits clear. A CRT monitor robot can hold the receipt and a code-plant garden reinforces that the main transaction is safely rooted; use a single clear receipt rather than duplicate coins to represent no double charge.
